notes_list.title: Carboxylic Acid Identification
notes_list.basic_overview: Carboxylic acids are acidic enough to react with bicarbonate/carbonate, releasing carbon dioxide gas.
notes_list.extra_info_content: The effervescence test is useful because many weaker organic acids do not liberate CO2 under the same conditions. Salt formation and acid-base extraction also exploit this property.
notes_list.conditions_and_medium: Aqueous bicarbonate/carbonate; observe gas evolution and confirm identity with additional tests if needed.
notes_list.mechanism_steps: Proton transfer to bicarbonate generates carbonic acid, which decomposes to CO2 and water.
notes_list.kinetics_and_energy: Acid-base reactions are rapid; gas evolution drives the equilibrium toward products.
notes_list.selectivity_and_stereochemistry: Used in qualitative analysis and separation schemes.
notes_list.common_traps: Phenols generally do not produce the same vigorous bicarbonate effervescence because they are weaker acids.

exam_focus.level: IIT-JAM / MSc entrance / GATE concept depth
